learner_facing_text: Hazards, exposure/conditions and controls affect risk; Crew Blueprint uses behavior as an instructional factor that can raise or lower exposure, not as a claim that OSHA codifies one universal hazard-risk-behavior taxonomy.
notes: Preserve the distinction between externally grounded risk concepts and Crew Blueprint's teaching model.

learner_facing_text: Notice, classify, control or escalate is a Crew Blueprint decision framework for recognizing conditions, taking only bounded action within the worker's role and reporting/escalating unresolved hazards; it is not a named OSHA doctrine.
notes: Near-miss reporting portion is externally supportable; NCCE naming/order is internal instructional architecture.

learner_facing_text: Fatigue, time pressure and reduced attention can increase error risk; the transferable learner behavior is to preserve control, communicate changing capability or uncertainty and use the controlling work/break/escalation process rather than hiding errors or improvising shortcuts.
notes: Exact break/rest rights and staffing decisions remain employer/CBA/jurisdiction specific.

learner_facing_text: Real event worksites can present multiple simultaneous hazards and controlled work zones; learners should identify what they can safely avoid/report, what requires site or department direction and what must be paused rather than guessed about.
notes: Do not teach a universal ranking of forklift, overhead, electrical or other hazards by job title alone; actual risk depends on context.

learner_facing_text: Call instructions, work phase, weather/site conditions and task hazards determine what clothing, PPE and readiness items are needed; show clothing and hazard-selected PPE can be separate requirements.
notes: Current examples such as hard hats, gloves or high-visibility clothing must remain task/site conditional rather than a universal kit.

learner_facing_text: Where required PPE applies to the assigned area or task, the learner should not perform that covered work without the required protection and controlling employer/site process; the course does not decide PPE solely from venue type or job title.
notes: Current list contains examples that need continued qualification; 'tall ceiling area' alone is not an OSHA head-protection trigger.

learner_facing_text: Clothing and PPE requirements can change across work phases, but an appearance direction does not itself prove that the underlying hazard assessment changed; the controlling employer/site hazard requirements and production dress requirements remain separate inputs.
notes: Current coaching sentence 'if production directs you to change, the hazard assessment changed' is too strong and should be revised later.

learner_facing_text: A general stagehand follows the assigned truck/dock unload order and does not bypass restraints, cargo-control decisions or loader direction on their own; Crew Blueprint does not teach one universal rear-to-front unloading law or cargo-securement method.
notes: Current lesson's universal physics/balance language is over-specific and should be revised after driver/loader practitioner review.

learner_facing_text: When an assigned manual movement task has limited visibility or a blind route, the worker should use the employer/lead's controlled movement method, added help or route adjustment rather than moving blindly; no universal two-person rule is asserted for every tall case.
notes: Current 'two-person standard' wording requires qualification because crew size/method depends on load, route, equipment and workplace process.

learner_facing_text: Team material handling requires deliberate coordination, clear stop/escalation behavior and body positioning appropriate to the actual load, route and assigned method; the course should not prescribe one universal ramp/body-position technique for every production load.
notes: Current detailed body-position and 'side pressure' instructions need adult practitioner/ergonomics review before stronger release.

learner_facing_text: Across dock-to-room material flow, a beginner's transferable responsibilities are following assigned workflow, preserving visibility and clear paths, respecting department ownership, confirming destinations and reporting completion rather than optimizing for individual speed.
notes: Exact truck, ramp, cable and public-route procedures remain task/site/system specific.

learner_facing_text: Recognizing, possessing or carrying a tool does not by itself authorize modifying another department's equipment or performing a controlled task; use remains limited to the assigned task and actual employer/lead authority.
notes: Strong authority-state concept; do not turn general tool familiarity into technical permission.

learner_facing_text: Obvious damage or abnormal condition should be reported and the affected item handled under the employer/department process rather than casually worked around; exact inspection and functional-test criteria remain equipment/model/task specific.
notes: Current universal 'there is always a replacement' and generic function-test wording should be revised; AI-generated road-case visual remains practitioner-review gated.

learner_facing_text: For coordinated handling, the team should use one clearly understood current-call method and stop when instructions conflict; exact caller placement, count-downs and vocabulary are crew/task specific rather than universal commands.
notes: Current exact command list and set-down sequence require qualification/practitioner review.

learner_facing_text: Assigned physical support and technical/system modification are different authority states. A general stagehand may support movement or setup under direction without gaining permission to connect, configure, troubleshoot or alter department systems.
notes: Exact permitted support varies by department, system, employer and assignment; avoid a universal 'can touch/cannot touch' object list.

learner_facing_text: Crew Blueprint's general-production, department, show-critical, performer-owned and exclusion categories are a decision aid for asking who controls an item or area; actual authority comes from the current assignment, department, employer, venue and external qualification rules where applicable.
notes: The categories help recognition but must not imply that every table, barricade, cable, deck piece or room has the same permission status on every call.

learner_facing_text: In mixed production spaces, learners should identify likely ownership/control and ask before changing uncertain department, performer-owned, energized, suspended or show-critical items rather than acting from familiarity alone.
notes: Current object-by-object examples require sector/practitioner review; no visual appearance can universally determine authority state.

learner_facing_text: Applicants should describe transferable experience and actual training honestly rather than converting observation or adjacent experience into claims of specialist competence; hiring requirements remain employer/local specific.
notes: Supports truthful skill-state representation and the backend need to distinguish experience, training, authorization and credentials.

learner_facing_text: Reliability, punctuality, professionalism, teamwork, safety and willingness to learn recur across hiring/local guidance as desirable worker behaviors, but Crew Blueprint should not present a universal callback score, guaranteed promotion sequence or fixed number of calls before better assignments.
notes: Current 'after 5–10 calls' specialization example is not established as a national rule and should be reframed later.

learner_facing_text: A responsible route toward specialization is to express interest, build relevant knowledge, accept appropriate support/supervised opportunities and obtain the actual employer/department/external authorization required for the next responsibility; self-study alone does not create work authority.
notes: Current wording that specialization begins only when 'invited' is too narrow; real pathways include hiring, training, apprenticeships, referrals and employer assignment.

learner_facing_text: Crew Blueprint recommends establishing preparation, communication, work-control, equipment awareness, feedback and department-boundary fundamentals early, but this is an instructional sequence rather than a universal probation period, promotion rule or required order for every worker.
notes: Current page already includes the key qualification that employer, venue, local and prior experience may set a different pace.
